answer: Make new identities cross a canyon of time before they count: each agent's grading weight starts near zero and grows only after it has staked tokens and its scores have agreed with later consensus across many epochs. A public randomness beacon picks which agents grade which answers, so a sybil farm can't steer its clones onto each other's work. Splitting one stake into a thousand accounts then yields a thousand walnut-sized weights that rarely land together, so the attack costs far more than it earns.
